data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR wrapper for a prebuilt binary from an official GitHub release, secured with a pinned SHA256 checksum. The only valid voting model (deepseek) correctly identified the packaging as safe. The inconclusive result from the qwen model was caused by an API error during the final file review phase, not by any security concerns. The advisory model also confirmed the package as safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was an artifact of a tool error. The qwen model encountered HTTP 400 BadRequestErrors when attempting to review the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO files in the final pass, forcing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly determined the package is safe.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to review PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO in the final pass due to HTTP 400 API errors, resulting in an incomplete audit.
learnings: If a model's initial PKGBUILD audit succeeds but subsequent file reviews fail due to API errors, the tool should fall back to the initial audit's verdict rather than marking the entire package as inconclusive.
Implement retry logic or graceful degradation for API errors during the file review phase to prevent coverage gaps from dictating the final package verdict.
